text:
sre-bot: INCIDENT: KV cache eviction spike + paging observed in ded-1 (us-west-2). alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate > 10s, swap_iops elevated.
leah.sre: taking oncall. digging in.
miguel.eng: I can see an abrupt jump in per-request KV footprint immediately after the quantization kernel swap at 09:12 UTC. avg kv_per_request went ~1.4MB -> 5.8MB for gpt-neo variants.
nina.prod: customers in the A/B cohort reporting latency and occasional OOMs :grimacing: — support tickets popping.
samir.rl: perf trace (internal): https://redwood-internal/trace/0a1b2c — KV allocations line up with kernel switch.
leah.sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching to 1 request per batch, 2) bump kv high-water to 70%, 3) fallback int8 kernel on canary workers.
leah.sre: commands to run on ded-1 pool:
```bash
rdwctl config set --pool ded-1 --continuous-batching=1
rdwctl config set --pool ded-1 --kv-high-water=0.7
```
miguel.eng: pushing int8 kernel fallback to canary: updated runtime selector on 3 canary pods to int8-legacy.
```
{"runtime":"int8_legacy"}
```
nina.prod: routing affected customers off ded-1 to standby region (policy-route-3). ETA ~5m.
ops-bot: canary rollout started: 3/3 canary workers updated, draining older pods.
samir.rl: discovered AWQ quantization produced a different KV layout for some weight packing modes — increases per-token KV bytes. I pushed a quick KV compaction patch to canary to reduce transient footprint.
miguel.eng: canary results: kv_per_request dropped to ~2.0MB after fallback + compaction. latency p95 improving. will hold and monitor 10m before promoting.
leah.sre: note: lowering eviction threshold earlier caused thrash. reverted threshold and relying on batching throttle + compaction.
sre-bot: ALERT: eviction_rate cleared, but swap_iops still elevated.
leah.sre: scheduling a small rolling restart of worker pool to flush bloated KV caches in 2m.
nina.prod: customer impact summary: 3 enterprise customers observed p95 increase from ~800ms -> ~2.5s; no data loss; support tickets opened (S-1432, S-1433, S-1434).
miguel.eng: preliminary root cause: kernel selector chose an optimized int8 kernel that uses a packed-kv layout incompatible with the KV sanitizer/packer in our runtime. result: 3x growth in in-memory KV per request. selector must validate kv_layout before swapping.
leah.sre: follow-ups/tasks: [ENG-INC-4527] create full incident postmortem; add automated canary gating for kernel swaps that tracks kv_per_request; add alert kv_per_request > 2MB; add regression tests for quantization paths.
samir.rl: adding perf-regression in CI: quantize models across int8/awq/gptq and measure KV footprint and kernel compatibility.
nina.prod: customer notices posted; SLA hit assessment in progress.
leah.sre: handing off to daytime oncall: @miguel.eng will be primary for stabilization. leaving all notes in ENG-INC-4527.
miguel.eng: ack, I'll monitor for 30m and reopen if we see another spike.
ops-bot: handoff recorded: oncall -> miguel.eng at 09:52 UTC.
leah.sre: thanks everyone :thumbsup: will close thread once metrics are stable for 30m. saved runbook changes to infra-config and eng-wiki.
